mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive quarterly GDPC1 declines.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% in a single month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 1% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of two consecutive months with INDPRO declines exceeding 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed 3% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average +10% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month is inconsistent with normal labor market dynamics and signals data noise or sectoral shifts, which increases uncertainty and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises while UNRATE rises in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS and UNRATE both rise in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month average by more than 15% for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which typically precedes a consumer spending slowdown and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average +15% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average by more than 15% for four consecutive months.
